submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on the head of a noun phrase that introduces a new, notable object, amount, or idea as the direct object of a verb: the article 'a' or a size or value adjective such as 'big' or 'low' ('a big hug', 'a low price', 'a good idea', 'a lot of tomatoes', 'a really special assignment'), and on the contracted negation "n't" after a modal or auxiliary marking a failed or refused action ('couldn't', 'didn't', 'wouldn't'). It stays quiet on ordinary content words and on affirmative, continuing narration. Token identity explains 37% of activation variance and the peak token itself drives the activation, while the vocabulary lens is incoherent (logit and Jacobian promoted lists share only 'OSE' and 'UE', agreement 20%), so there is no lookahead signal.
